title: AWS CloudFormation now simplifies stack update rollback operations
summary: Discover more about what's new at AWS with AWS CloudFormation now simplifies stack update rollback operations
body_markdown:
[AWS CloudFormation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cloudformation/) now makes it simpler to complete an update rollback and get back to deploying. An update rollback returns your stack to a known good state. Starting today, if some resources cannot roll back automatically, force rollback enables you to complete the rollback in a single operation. It works across every CloudFormation workflow, from the[AWS CLI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/cloudformation/) , and SDKs to[AWS CDK](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cdk/v2/guide/) and AI agents.


With force rollback, CloudFormation completes the update rollback and returns your stack to a deployable state in a single operation, instead of requiring you to identify, list, and retry the operation for each affected resource. Any resource that still needs attention, such as one affected by a change outside CloudFormation, is recorded for you to review and resolve it before your next deployment.


To get started, run continue update rollback with the force rollback option, then create a[drift-aware change set](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/drift-aware-change-sets.html) to review any configuration differences before your next deployment. To learn more, see[Continue rolling back an update](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/using-cfn-updating-stacks-continueupdaterollback.html) in the AWS CloudFormation User Guide.


Force rollback is available in all Regions at no additional cost. Refer to the[AWS Region table](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/cfn.html#cfn_region) for service availability details.
